findings.title: An offline rename of a pendingInit workspace is now lost if its folder comes back with an identity from another Mac
findings.body: `edit` now keeps `pendingInit` when the folder could not be written (line 634), and sets `pendingIdentity` (line 638). Suppose the folder later comes back holding an `identity.json` with an id this Mac doesn't know. `availability` then takes the adoption branch (lines 718-727): `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))` replaces the name, color and initials with the folder's values, and `pendingIdentity` is never consulted. The user's rename is gone, and nothing tells them. Before this change `pendingInit` was cleared, so the same folder was reported as `different` instead. This takes a drive that was away at upgrade, a rename while it was away, and another Mac writing an identity in the meantime, which is the follow-up you already noted on the earlier thread. If you want to keep the rename, the adoption branch could re-apply `name`/`color`/`initials` and keep `pendingIdentity` when the entry has it, so the next probe writes them to the file.

findings.title: No renderer test pins that an unchanged relocate shows no toast
findings.body: The `unchanged` flag is asserted only in main (`relocate.test.ts:158`). Nothing under `features/workspaces` checks `result.unchanged`: a search finds the flag only on this line. So if this early return were dropped, the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back and every test would still pass. A provider test where `workspaces.relocate` resolves `{ ok: true, unchanged: true, workspace }` and no toast appears would cover it, ideally next to the existing changed case that shows `folderChanged`.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: the rollback calls `removeIdentity` when `previous` was absent (registry.ts:645-646). It also still restores the old file when there was one.
Confirmed: the name check runs again inside the locked `update` (registry.ts:626) and is reported as `name-taken`.

Confirmed: `checkRelocate` accepts a folder with Kaipu items and no identity for a `pendingInit` entry (registry.ts:855). `edit` no longer clears `pendingInit` while the folder is away, and the new test covers that path. The case where the folder holds a different id stays as the follow-up you noted.
Confirmed: name and color are now checked separately (index.ts:273-274).
Confirmed: when the picked folder is the current one, `relocateWorkspace` returns before `relocateActive` (relocate.ts:43-45). The test shows the log stays empty and the generation stays at 1.

Confirmed: `unchanged: true` goes from relocate.ts through index.ts:349 to the renderer, which skips the toast (workspaces-context.tsx:168). One nit: the renderer side has no test yet (see the new comment).

structuredOutput.summary:
I reviewed the 7 files in this push. It does two things. It adds an `unchanged` flag, so picking the folder the workspace already uses no longer shows the "now points to the new folder" toast. And `edit` now keeps `pendingInit` when it couldn't write to the folder, so "Change folder…" still accepts the moved folder later.

Both changes are correct for the cases they target. The new registry test and the updated relocate test check the right things.

Two "consider" findings, nothing blocking:
- **Lost rename (registry.ts:634):** because `pendingInit` is now kept, there is a rare way to lose an offline rename. If the folder comes back holding an identity written by another Mac, the probe adopts it and replaces the name and color the user chose, with no message.
- **Missing test (workspaces-context.tsx:168):** no renderer test checks that the toast is skipped when the folder didn't change.

All six earlier threads on these files are addressed in the current code.
